transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm coming in because I feel completely overwhelmed and exhausted, and my mind has been racing constantly. I've also been hearing voices that others can't hear, and these struggles have been going on for nearly two years now. It
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing voices or having other psychotic symptoms even though your mood felt normal, without racing thoughts, depression, or mania?

Yes, absolutely. There have been times, especially over the last year, where my mood felt completely stable and normal, but I was still hearing those voices and believing that I was being monitored. It lasted for at least a few weeks during those quiet periods, even when my energy wasn't high at all.
Have you also had clear episodes of mania or major depression that lasted most of the day for at least a week for mania or two weeks for depression, separate from the times you were hearing voices?

Yes, I've had a period of intense mania that lasted for about five months where my energy was incredibly high and my thoughts were racing constantly. During most of that time, I was also hearing the voices and feeling monitored, so those symptoms overlapped. But as I mentioned, there were definitely other times where the voices stayed even after that high energy completely faded away.
Have you had any major depressive episodes as well, with low mood or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks?
No, I haven't really experienced any periods of low mood or losing interest in things. My mood is usually either very high and energetic, or it just feels normal. I've never felt depressed like that.

Based on your history, the most likely diagnosis is schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type. Before we finish, have you ever had hallucinations or delusions for at least two weeks when you were not having any mood symptoms at all?

Yes, I have. There were definitely times lasting at least two or three weeks where my mood felt completely stable and normal, but I still heard the voices and felt like I was being watched. I didn't have any of that high energy or racing thoughts during those periods.

Schizophrenia remains on the list because there are persistent psychotic symptoms outside mood episodes, but the presence of a distinct prolonged manic episode means schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type is more likely than schizophrenia.

Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) remains possible because of psychosis with possible manic-spectrum symptoms (racing thoughts), Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features remains possible if the psychosis occurs only during mood episodes, and Schizophrenia remains possible because psychotic symptoms have persisted for a long duration. There is not enough information yet to distinguish mood-episode timing, duration of mood symptoms, or functional decline.
